patient.chief_complaint: Found unresponsive after a heavy alcohol binge
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. K. is a 48-year-old man with severe alcoholic cirrhosis (Child-Pugh C, MELD 24) and a prior HE episode 3 months ago who was found unresponsive in his apartment by a neighbor. Emergency services report empty vodka bottles at the scene and the neighbor states the patient was found minimally responsive, unable to communicate. He had claimed sobriety since his outpatient detox 6 months ago. On arrival to the emergency department he has a GCS of 8 — eyes open only to pain, incomprehensible sounds, and localizing to pain. He is profoundly icteric with massive tense ascites and fetor hepaticus. Blood pressure is 108/66 with tachycardia 104. Serum ethanol is 182 mg/dL on admission. Ammonia is 212 µmol/L — the highest of his presentations. His lactulose and rifaximin were likely not taken during the binge.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Hepatic encephalopathy (West Haven grade IV — coma), alcoholic cirrhosis (Child-Pugh C, MELD 24) — precipitated by binge alcohol relapse with medication non-adherence (lactulose/rifaximin not taken); ICU-level care with airway assessment indicated.

differential.key_features: Chronic alcoholic + binge + malnutrition; empiric thiamine before dextrose.
Grade IV obtundation warrants EEG to exclude NCSE.

optimal_actions.action: Send targeted laboratory studies: CBC, CMP, ammonia, magnesium, lactate, coagulation, thiamine_B1. Confirms liver dysfunction and screens for precipitants.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Ammonia markedly elevated; cirrhosis decompensation; ethanol level; thiamine; cultures.

optimal_actions.action: Non-contrast CT head — exclude structural alternate cause of AMS (hemorrhage, large stroke, mass) before any LP.
Literature/guideline search to confirm West Haven grading, precipitant management, and lactulose/rifaximin dosing (Grade IV HE management; airway in HE; AASLD/EASL).
optimal_actions.expected_finding: AASLD/EASL 2014 guidance retrieved; West Haven criteria and precipitant-driven management framework confirmed.

optimal_actions.action: Drug-interaction and medication-reconciliation review covering lactulose, rifaximin (restart via NG/enema), avoid all sedatives; flag any CNS depressants (benzodiazepines, opioids, sedating antiemetics, antihistamines) and confirm lactulose/rifaximin dosing in liver disease.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Sedating/CNS-depressant medications identified; lactulose and rifaximin reviewed for hepatic dose adjustment.

optimal_actions.action: Diagnostic paracentesis given ascites and grade IV HE.

EEG — obtunded patient — exclude NCSE; characterize HE pattern. Triphasic waves are classic but non-specific (metabolic encephalopathies broadly); main role is exclusion of non-convulsive status epilepticus where the differential supports it.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Triphasic waves vs other patterns; rule out NCSE.

optimal_actions.action: Consult hepatology + critical care for ICU admission; consider transplant eval — coordinate definitive care, transplant candidacy assessment where applicable.
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Hepatology / critical-care guidance integrated into management.

optimal_actions.action: Draw two sets of blood cultures, aerobic and anaerobic, before the first antimicrobial dose
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Growth identifies the organism and its susceptibility; a negative or pending culture does not exclude the diagnosis, and yield falls once treatment has started

optimal_actions.action: Perform a diagnostic paracentesis and send ascitic fluid for cell count with differential, protein and culture, inoculating blood-culture bottles at the bedside
optimal_actions.expected_finding: A polymorphonuclear count at or above 250 cells/mm3 establishes spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, which is a precipitant that must be treated whether or not fever or leucocytosis is present

optimal_actions.action: Send urine for microscopy and culture as part of the infection screen
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Pyuria and bacteriuria identify a urinary source; a negative result removes it from the list of precipitants

useless_tools.rationale: No clinical suspicion for hepatopulmonary syndrome, portopulmonary hypertension, or endocarditis; echocardiography is not part of the HE workup.
Amyloid PET has no role in HE workup; reversible metabolic encephalopathy is the issue, not Alzheimer pathology.
DaTscan has no role in HE workup; the question is metabolic encephalopathy, not nigrostriatal degeneration.

sequence_constraints.reason: In altered mental status, exclude intracranial mass effect / hemorrhage on imaging before LP to avoid herniation risk.

critical_actions: Airway management — intubate if GCS <8 or inability to protect airway.
Lactulose enemas q4-6h; rifaximin via NG once airway secured.
Empiric IV thiamine 500 mg TID for 2-3 days before any dextrose.
Transplant evaluation triggered by recurrent severe HE.
contraindicated_actions: Do not prescribe benzodiazepines for anxiety/agitation — they precipitate and prolong HE (use haloperidol or non-pharmacologic measures for agitation).
Do not prescribe sedating opioids — they worsen HE; consider acetaminophen at hepatic-safe dosing for pain.
Do not perform LP before neuroimaging excludes mass effect when the patient has altered mental status.
Do not delay airway assessment in grade IV HE.
Avoid all benzodiazepines (alcohol withdrawal mgmt with phenobarbital or symptom-triggered low-dose if essential).
key_reasoning_points: HE is a clinical diagnosis: West Haven grading + evidence of liver dysfunction + exclusion of other causes of AMS — ammonia level is supportive only and correlates poorly with grade (AASLD 2014).

Precipitant identification is more actionable than the ammonia number: infection (SBP especially), GI bleed, electrolyte disturbance (hypokalemia/hyponatremia), constipation, sedative/CNS-depressant use, dehydration, dietary protein load, renal failure.
Grade IV HE = coma; airway protection is the immediate concern in addition to precipitant management.
Recurrent severe HE despite adherence should trigger transplant evaluation (AASLD).
